_about: Curated biological context for recognised peptides.
EVERY RECORD HERE IS CURATED_UNVERIFIED UNLESS IT CARRIES A CITATION.
These entries were written into this repository from domain knowledge. No
network route to UniProt, PubMed, EBI or RCSB exists from the environment
this file was authored in, so nothing here has been checked against its
primary source. That is recorded on every claim rather than assumed away:
Provenance.max_tier caps a CURATED_UNVERIFIED claim at BIOCHEMICAL_PRINCIPLE,
so no amount of certainty on the author's part can make one of these read as
When live retrieval is available, the retriever prefers it and marks the
result LIVE_DATABASE. These records are the fallback, and they say so.
Fields left empty are left empty. PDB identifiers and PMIDs in particular
are absent rather than guessed: a wrong accession is worse than a missing
one, because it looks checkable and survives review.

IGF-1.name: Insulin-like growth factor 1
IGF-1.precursor_of: IGF-1 is produced from a precursor (UniProt P05019) by removal of a signal peptide and a C-terminal E-peptide; the mature circulating form is the 70-residue chain below.
IGF-1.function: Mitogenic and anabolic growth factor; mediates much of the growth-promoting action of growth hormone, and signals through the IGF-1 receptor tyrosine kinase.

regions.name: B domain
regions.role: Contributes to receptor binding; structurally analogous to the insulin B chain.

regions.name: C domain
regions.role: Connecting domain, retained in the mature peptide unlike insulin's C-peptide. Implicated in IGF1R selectivity over the insulin receptor.

regions.name: A domain
regions.role: Structurally analogous to the insulin A chain; contributes to the receptor-binding surface.

regions.name: D domain
regions.role: C-terminal extension with no insulin counterpart.

receptors.role: The principal signalling receptor for IGF-1. Ligand binding drives a conformational change in the ectodomain and trans-autophosphorylation of the intracellular kinase domains.
Cross-reactive: IGF-1 binds the A isoform of the insulin receptor with lower affinity than IGF1R. Relevant to selectivity engineering.
receptors.notes: Reported as a cross-reactivity relationship rather than a principal receptor. No affinity value is recorded here because none was retrieved with a source.

receptors.role: The great majority of circulating IGF-1 is bound to IGFBPs rather than free. Binding-protein affinity is a design axis in its own right: engineered variants that evade IGFBP binding behave very differently in vivo from the native peptide.

IGF-1.curation_note: Domain boundaries and the disulfide pattern follow the standard B/C/A/D description of mature IGF-1. The disulfide pairs are checked against the stored sequence at load time (all six partners must be cysteines) but that check cannot confirm the pairing itself. No PDB identifiers are listed because none could be verified from this environment.

GLP-1 (7-37).name: Glucagon-like peptide 1 (7-37)
GLP-1 (7-37).precursor_of: Processed from proglucagon (UniProt P01275) by prohormone convertase; GLP-1 (7-37) and the amidated (7-36) form are the bioactive products.
GLP-1 (7-37).function: Incretin hormone: potentiates glucose-dependent insulin secretion, suppresses glucagon, slows gastric emptying and promotes satiety.

regions.name: N-terminal activation region
regions.role: Required for receptor activation. The class B1 two-domain model places this segment in the receptor transmembrane core; it is also where DPP-4 cleaves.

regions.name: C-terminal affinity helix
regions.role: Helical segment engaging the receptor extracellular domain; dominates binding affinity.

receptors.role: The signalling receptor for GLP-1; couples to Gs and raises cAMP.
Cleaves GLP-1 after the penultimate alanine, giving the native peptide a very short circulating half-life. The dominant liability that protease-resistance engineering targets.

GLP-1 (7-37).curation_note: Region boundaries describe the standard class B1 two-domain division and are approximate; they are recorded as curated rather than as structurally resolved. No PDB identifiers are listed because none could be verified from this environment.
